Well, the first step for a home-bartender would be an idea of the kind of drinks you're going to want to make. Once you have recipes in mind, you can stock your liquor cabinet accordingly. Be sure you know about the right kinds of mixers to get, and don't leave out any ingredients.

As far as basic equipment goes, I'd start with:

  • Mixing tin (Boston Shaker
  • Muddler (wooden)
  • Hawthorne Strainer
  • Good Sharp Knife
  • Jigger
  • Pour Spouts
  • Appropriate Glassware

Very soon I will be posting a detailed list of equipment/glassware with descriptions and explanations, keep an eye out for it - It will be very helpful for those looking to start out in the trade.

These aren't all the tools of the trade, per se; but they'll get you started.

As far as ideas for drinks, just take a look at some of the ideas submitted by users here, in both posts and comments. If there's a specific type of liquor that you like; and you want suggestions - post a request for ideas.

The skills come with time, and if you have trouble with any one aspect of making a drink, let us know, and someone here will be able to walk you through the process, or link you to a helpful video.

Thanks for your query. Byr

Hey and welcome! When I first started bartending years ago, I started with a basic kit that I always carried with me to catering jobs. It was a shaker, strainer, jigger, and a few pourspouts. Since then, I've upgraded but it doesn't take much more than that when starting out. I second the muddler and knife, though. Many days on the job, the "bar knife" was about as sharp as a potato and my lemons and limes suffered immense torture as i pretty much tried to spatula them into wedges and wheels.

Also!! When experimenting with something new, start small. Divide the recipe in half, or 1/4th and make just a small amount of a cocktail so you can play with the levels of flavor without needing to add more than a few drops of any ingredient. Make mental notes as you go until you have the flavors perfect, then try to recreate the same balance of flavors in a full size cocktail.

Cheers!!
